intro: Welcome to C1! At B2 you started sentences with -ing, V3 and Having + V3: Walking home, I saw Rina. Having finished the report, I went home. Today you go further: Having been told the news, she… / Founded in 2015, the startup… / With prices rising, people… And you'll learn to spot the funny mistake in 'Arriving late, the meeting had already started'.
teachingNotes: Recap b2-participle-clauses in one or two lines, don't re-teach it: -ing clauses (same time / reason), V3 clauses with a passive meaning (Built in 1990, …), Having + V3 for an earlier action, Not + -ing, after/before + -ing, and the basic same-subject rule. New here: (1) the perfect PASSIVE participle having been + V3 (Having been told the news, she started to cry; Having been rejected twice, he…), its negative Not having been + V3, and the active/passive contrast; (2) V3 clauses that pack background facts into the start of a sentence (Built in 1920, the station…; Founded in 2015 by two ITB graduates, the startup…); (3) with/without + noun + -ing/-ed; (4) dangling participles in detail, including passive main clauses.

Common error 2 (THE key contrast of objective perfect-passive-participles): *Having told the news, she started to cry → Having been told the news, she started to cry. Having told = she told someone (active, ≈ setelah memberi tahu); Having been told = someone told her (passive, ≈ setelah diberi tahu). Bridge: having + V3 ≈ sudah me-, having been + V3 ≈ sudah di-. Negative: not goes first: Not having received a reply, I… (active, recap) / Not having been invited, Budi… (passive), never *Not been invited. (Having not been + V3 also exists but is less common: accept it, don't teach or test it.) Test active vs passive with clear contexts. Do NOT make 'Rejected twice, …' vs 'Having been rejected twice, …' an either-or question: both are correct; the bare V3 is more common for facts and descriptions (Built in 1920, …), having been + V3 stresses that the passive event came first and often gives a reason. Being + V3 (Being watched, …) is outside this lesson: accept it if correct, don't teach it.

Objective with-noun-ing: with + noun + -ing gives background or a cause that is still going on (With prices rising, people are buying less = because prices are rising; With the deadline approaching, the team worked late); with + noun + V3 gives a finished state (With the report finished, we went for dinner = now that the report was finished); without + noun + -ing (Without anyone noticing, Rina left the room). The with-clause has its OWN subject (prices, the deadline, anyone), so it does NOT have to match the main subject and is not a dangling participle; say this explicitly. Common error 3: a finite verb after with, from Indonesian 'dengan harga yang terus naik': *With the prices rise / *With prices are rising → With prices rising. Also mention that general 'prices' needs no 'the' (the price of rice is specific). Register: with + noun + -ing is common in news, reports AND speech.

Objective avoid-dangling-participles (common error 1): the hidden subject of the participle must be the subject of the main clause, the first noun/pronoun after the comma: *Arriving late, the meeting had already started (the meeting didn't arrive) → Arriving late, I found that the meeting had already started / When I arrived, the meeting had already started. Two fixes: change the main subject to the real doer, or use a full clause with its own subject (When I arrived…, After the technician had fixed it…). Big C1 trap: a passive main clause, very common in Indonesian-style report writing (Setelah dicek, laporan dikirim): *Having checked the figures, the report was sent → Having checked the figures, we sent the report. Also V3 clauses dangle: *Built in 1920, my grandfather worked at the station. Indonesian trap: Indonesian lets the subject float ('Setelah tiba, rapat sudah dimulai' sounds fine), so learners must check every time. Use funny wrong examples; they stick.

Honest exceptions: a few fixed phrases are accepted even though their 'doer' is the speaker, not the main subject: Generally speaking, …; Judging by …; Considering …; Given … (Judging by the queue, the new café is popular). Treat them as phrases to remember; don't test them. Register: participle clauses (especially having been + V3) are mostly formal writing (reports, news, essays, CVs); in speech full clauses are normal, and a correct full clause is a right answer unless the task asks for a participle clause.

Limits: no inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive or impersonal passive (It is said that…) in examples. Result clauses (…, causing delays) and Being + V3 are not taught here. Contexts: offices, ministries, startups, NGOs, universities, news and reports in Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, Yogyakarta. Spelling: British organisation/practise; American organization/practice; both accepted.

keyPoints.title: Having + V3 vs Having been + V3
keyPoints.explanation: Having + V3 = the subject DID something first (active): Having told her manager, Rina felt better. Having been + V3 = something was DONE TO the subject first (passive): Having been told the news, she started to cry (someone told her). The negative puts not first: Not having been invited, Budi didn't know about the decision. A plain V3 can also start a sentence with background facts: Built in 1920, the station is now a museum.

examples.en: Having been told the news, she started to cry.
examples.id: Setelah diberi tahu kabar itu, dia mulai menangis.

examples.en: Having told her manager, Rina felt much better.
examples.id: Setelah memberi tahu atasannya, Rina merasa jauh lebih lega.

examples.en: Founded in 2015, the startup now employs 200 people.
examples.id: Didirikan tahun 2015, startup itu kini mempekerjakan 200 orang.

id.title: Having + V3 vs Having been + V3
id.explanation: Having + V3 = subjek SUDAH MELAKUKAN sesuatu lebih dulu (aktif, ≈ sudah me-): Having told her manager, Rina felt better. Having been + V3 = subjek SUDAH DIKENAI tindakan lebih dulu (pasif, ≈ sudah di-): Having been told the news, she started to cry (ada orang yang memberi tahu dia). Bentuk negatif: not di depan: Not having been invited, Budi didn't know about the decision. V3 saja juga bisa membuka kalimat dengan fakta latar: Built in 1920, the station is now a museum.

keyPoints.title: with / without + noun + -ing or V3
keyPoints.explanation: Use with + noun + -ing for background or a cause that is still going on: With prices rising, people are buying less. Use with + noun + V3 for something already done: With the report finished, we went for dinner. Without + noun + -ing: Without anyone noticing, Rina left the room. After with, never a full verb: 'With the prices rise' is wrong. The noun after with is the doer of the -ing, so it doesn't have to be the main subject.

examples.en: With prices rising, people are buying less.
examples.id: Karena harga-harga terus naik, orang-orang membeli lebih sedikit.

examples.en: With the report finished, we went out for dinner.
examples.id: Karena laporannya sudah selesai, kami pergi makan malam.

examples.en: Without anyone noticing, Rina left the room.
examples.id: Tanpa ada yang menyadari, Rina keluar dari ruangan.

id.title: with / without + kata benda + -ing atau V3
id.explanation: Pakai with + kata benda + -ing untuk latar atau sebab yang masih berlangsung: With prices rising, people are buying less. Pakai with + kata benda + V3 untuk sesuatu yang sudah selesai: With the report finished, we went for dinner. Without + kata benda + -ing: Without anyone noticing, Rina left the room. Setelah with, jangan pakai kata kerja lengkap: 'With the prices rise' salah. Kata benda setelah with adalah pelaku -ing-nya, jadi tidak harus sama dengan subjek utama.

keyPoints.title: No dangling participles
keyPoints.explanation: The hidden subject of the participle must be the subject of the main clause (the first noun or pronoun after the comma). 'Arriving late, the meeting had already started' is wrong: the meeting didn't arrive late. Fix it by changing the main subject (Arriving late, I found that the meeting had already started) or by using a full clause (When I arrived, the meeting had already started). Watch passive main clauses: 'Having checked the figures, the report was sent' is wrong too.

examples.en: Arriving late, I found that the meeting had already started.
examples.id: Karena datang terlambat, saya mendapati rapat sudah dimulai.

examples.en: When I arrived, the meeting had already started.
examples.id: Saat saya tiba, rapat sudah dimulai.

id.title: Hindari dangling participle
id.explanation: Subjek tersembunyi dari partisip harus sama dengan subjek klausa utama (kata benda atau kata ganti pertama setelah koma). 'Arriving late, the meeting had already started' salah: rapatnya tidak datang terlambat. Perbaiki dengan mengganti subjek utama (Arriving late, I found that the meeting had already started) atau dengan klausa lengkap (When I arrived, the meeting had already started). Hati-hati dengan klausa utama pasif: 'Having checked the figures, the report was sent' juga salah.

assessment.prompt: Write having or having been in the gap: ___ promoted to team leader in March, Sari now manages a team of eight.
assessment.rubric: Correct: having been (Sari was promoted by the company: passive, ≈ sudah dipromosikan). 'having' = 0 ('Having promoted' would mean Sari promoted someone else). 'being' = 30 (passive idea but not the earlier, finished action). Leaving the gap empty (Promoted to team leader in March, …) = 60: correct English, but the task asks for having or having been.

assessment.prompt: Complete with having or having been + the verb in brackets: ___ (sign) the partnership agreement, the two companies held a joint press conference in Jakarta.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Having signed (the companies did the signing first: active, ≈ setelah menandatangani). 'Having been signed' = 0 (the companies weren't signed). 'Having sign' = 30 (needs the V3). 'After signing' = 60 (correct English, but the task asks for having + V3).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word made from the verb in brackets: ___ (design) by a Dutch architect in the 1920s, the old building on our street is now a popular café.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Designed (the building was designed: passive meaning, V3, background fact). 'Designing' = 0 (the building didn't design anything). 'Design' = 0. 'Having been designed' = 70 (correct, but the task asks for one word).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word made from the verb in brackets: With unemployment ___ (fall) for the third year in a row, the government is under less pressure to create jobs.
assessment.rubric: Correct: falling (with + noun + -ing: unemployment is still falling). 'falls' or 'fell' = 10 (a full verb can't follow with + noun). 'fallen' = 30 (fall can't be passive; 'has fallen' would need a full clause). 'fall' = 0.

acceptableAnswers: with interest rates going up again many young couples are postponing their plans to buy a house

assessment.prompt:
Which sentence has NO dangling participle? Write A, B or C.
A: Stuck in traffic for two hours, the meeting started without me.
B: Stuck in traffic for two hours, the client was told that I would be late.
C: Stuck in traffic for two hours, I missed the start of the meeting.
assessment.rubric: Correct: C (I was stuck in traffic, and I is the subject after the comma). A = 0 (says the meeting was stuck in traffic). B = 0 (says the client was stuck in traffic: the passive main clause makes the client the subject).

assessment.prompt:
Fix the dangling participle. Keep the start 'Having finished the survey,' and make the team the subject of the main clause:
Having finished the survey, the results were sent to the ministry by the team.
acceptableAnswers: having finished the survey the team sent the results to the ministry
the team sent the results to the ministry
having finished the survey the team sent its results to the ministry
having finished the survey the team sent their results to the ministry

having finished the survey the team then sent the results to the ministry
assessment.rubric: Correct: Having finished the survey, the team sent the results to the ministry (the team finished the survey, so the team comes right after the comma, in an active main clause). 'its'/'their results' = fine. A full clause instead (After the team had finished the survey, the results were sent…) = 70 (correct English, but the task says keep the start). Keeping the passive 'the results were sent' = 0 (the results didn't finish the survey). Wrong tense of send (sends/has sent) = 70.

material.title: From Having + V3 to Having been + V3

blocks.text:
**Quick recap (B2):** a participle clause starts a sentence with **-ing** (*Walking home, I saw Rina*), a **V3** with a passive meaning (*Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong*) or **Having + V3** for an earlier action (*Having finished the report, I went home*). The subject after the comma must be the one doing it.
**New at C1: the passive version, having been + V3.** Compare:
- ***Having told** her manager, Rina felt much better.* = Rina told her manager (she **did** it: active, ≈ *setelah memberi tahu*).
- ***Having been told** the news, she started to cry.* = Someone told her (it was **done to** her: passive, ≈ *setelah diberi tahu*).
**Perfect** means the action was finished **before** the main action. **Passive** means the subject receives the action. So *having been + V3* = 'after/because the subject had been ___ed'.
**Negative:** put **not** first: *Not having received a reply, I called again* (active, you met it at B2) → ***Not having been invited**, Budi didn't know about the decision* (passive).
**Common mistake:** *'Having told the news, she started to cry'* ✗. That says **she** told someone the news. If she heard it, she **was told**: ***Having been told** the news, …* ✓

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat (B2):** klausa partisip membuka kalimat dengan **-ing** (*Walking home, I saw Rina*), **V3** bermakna pasif (*Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong*), atau **Having + V3** untuk kegiatan yang lebih dulu (*Having finished the report, I went home*). Subjek setelah koma harus yang melakukannya.
**Baru di C1: versi pasifnya, having been + V3.** Bandingkan:
- ***Having told** her manager, Rina felt much better.* = Rina memberi tahu atasannya (dia **melakukan**: aktif, ≈ *setelah memberi tahu*).
- ***Having been told** the news, she started to cry.* = Ada orang yang memberi tahu dia (dia **dikenai** tindakan: pasif, ≈ *setelah diberi tahu*).
**Perfect** artinya kegiatannya sudah selesai **sebelum** kegiatan utama. **Pasif** artinya subjek menerima tindakan. Jadi *having been + V3* = 'setelah/karena subjek sudah di-___'.
**Negatif:** taruh **not** di depan: *Not having received a reply, I called again* (aktif, sudah kamu temui di B2) → ***Not having been invited**, Budi didn't know about the decision* (pasif).
**Kesalahan umum:** *'Having told the news, she started to cry'* ✗. Kalimat ini berarti **dia** yang memberi tahu orang lain. Kalau dia yang mendengar kabarnya, dia **was told** (diberi tahu): ***Having been told** the news, …* ✓

rows.en: Having told her manager, Rina felt much better.
rows.id: Setelah memberi tahu atasannya, Rina merasa jauh lebih lega.

rows.en: Having been told the news, she started to cry.
rows.id: Setelah diberi tahu kabar itu, dia mulai menangis.

rows.en: Having been rejected twice, Dimas almost gave up on his startup idea.
rows.id: Karena sudah dua kali ditolak, Dimas hampir menyerah pada ide startup-nya.

rows.en: Not having been invited, Budi didn't know about the decision.
rows.id: Karena tidak diundang, Budi tidak tahu soal keputusan itu.

blocks.text: **Indonesian bridge:** *having + V3* ≈ **sudah me-** (*setelah menandatangani* → *having signed*); *having been + V3* ≈ **sudah di-** (*setelah diberi tahu* → *having been told*). If your Indonesian sentence has **di-**, you probably need **been**.

id.text: **Jembatan dari bahasa Indonesia:** *having + V3* ≈ **sudah me-** (*setelah menandatangani* → *having signed*); *having been + V3* ≈ **sudah di-** (*setelah diberi tahu* → *having been told*). Kalau kalimat Indonesiamu memakai **di-**, kemungkinan besar kamu butuh **been**.

blocks.prompt: ___ by the ministry, the NGO started the project in three villages in East Java.
blocks.explain: The NGO didn't approve anything; it was approved by the ministry (disetujui). Passive + earlier → Having been approved. 'Having approving' isn't a form.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ by the ministry, the NGO started the project in three villages in East Java.
id.explain: LSM itu tidak menyetujui apa pun; LSM itu disetujui oleh kementerian. Pasif + lebih dulu → Having been approved. 'Having approving' bukan bentuk yang benar.

id.title: Dari Having + V3 ke Having been + V3

material.title: V3 at the start: background facts

blocks.text:
Reports, news and company profiles often pack **background facts** into a V3 clause at the start, so the main clause can say what matters now:
- ***Built** in 1920, the station is now a museum.* (= The station was built in 1920. It is now a museum.)
- ***Founded** in 2015 by two ITB graduates, the startup now employs 200 people.*
- ***Funded** by an Australian partner, the programme trains 500 teachers a year.*
**V3 alone or having been + V3?** Both can be right: *Rejected twice, Dimas almost gave up* and *Having been rejected twice, Dimas almost gave up* mean nearly the same. The **plain V3 is more common for facts and descriptions** (built, founded, located, written). **Having been** stresses that the passive event happened **first** and often gives a **reason**. It's a style choice, not a right/wrong one.
The subject rule still applies: the thing that was built/founded must come right after the comma. *'Built in 1920, my grandfather worked at the station'* ✗ (your grandfather wasn't built in 1920!).

id.text:
Laporan, berita dan profil perusahaan sering memadatkan **fakta latar** ke dalam klausa V3 di awal kalimat, supaya klausa utama bisa fokus pada hal yang penting sekarang:
- ***Built** in 1920, the station is now a museum.* (= Stasiun itu dibangun tahun 1920. Sekarang jadi museum.)
- ***Founded** in 2015 by two ITB graduates, the startup now employs 200 people.*
- ***Funded** by an Australian partner, the programme trains 500 teachers a year.*
**V3 saja atau having been + V3?** Keduanya bisa benar: *Rejected twice, Dimas almost gave up* dan *Having been rejected twice, Dimas almost gave up* artinya hampir sama. **V3 saja lebih umum untuk fakta dan deskripsi** (built, founded, located, written). **Having been** menegaskan bahwa kejadian pasif itu terjadi **lebih dulu** dan sering memberi **alasan**. Ini soal gaya, bukan benar/salah.
Aturan subjek tetap berlaku: benda yang dibangun/didirikan harus ada tepat setelah koma. *'Built in 1920, my grandfather worked at the station'* ✗ (kakekmu tidak dibangun tahun 1920!).

rows.en: Built in 1920, the station is now a museum.
rows.id: Dibangun tahun 1920, stasiun itu kini menjadi museum.

rows.en: Founded in 2015 by two ITB graduates, the startup now employs 200 people.
rows.id: Didirikan tahun 2015 oleh dua lulusan ITB, startup itu kini mempekerjakan 200 orang.

id.note: fakta latar + hal yang penting sekarang

blocks.text:
**with + noun + -ing** adds background or a **cause that is still going on**. It's common in news, reports and in speech too:
- ***With prices rising**, people are buying less.* (= because prices are rising)
- ***With the deadline approaching**, the whole team worked late.*
**with + noun + V3** = something is **already done** (passive or finished):
- ***With the report finished**, we went out for dinner.* (= now that the report was finished)
**without + noun + -ing:**
- ***Without anyone noticing**, Rina left the room.*
**Why isn't this a dangling participle?** Because the with-clause has its **own subject**: *prices* are rising, *the deadline* is approaching, *anyone* didn't notice. So it doesn't have to match the main subject. That's exactly why it's useful when the two doers are different.
**Common mistake:** a full verb after with: *'With the prices rise'* ✗, *'With prices are rising'* ✗ → ***With prices rising*** ✓. Note also: *prices* in general takes no *the* (but *the price of rice* is specific).

id.text:
**with + kata benda + -ing** menambahkan latar atau **sebab yang masih berlangsung**. Bentuk ini umum di berita, laporan, dan juga percakapan:
- ***With prices rising**, people are buying less.* (= karena harga-harga sedang naik)
- ***With the deadline approaching**, the whole team worked late.*
**with + kata benda + V3** = sesuatu **sudah selesai** (pasif atau tuntas):
- ***With the report finished**, we went out for dinner.* (= karena laporannya sudah selesai)
**without + kata benda + -ing:**
- ***Without anyone noticing**, Rina left the room.*
**Kenapa ini bukan dangling participle?** Karena klausa with punya **subjeknya sendiri**: *prices* yang naik, *the deadline* yang mendekat, *anyone* yang tidak menyadari. Jadi tidak harus sama dengan subjek utama. Justru karena itu bentuk ini berguna kalau pelakunya berbeda.
**Kesalahan umum:** kata kerja lengkap setelah with: *'With the prices rise'* ✗, *'With prices are rising'* ✗ → ***With prices rising*** ✓. Perhatikan juga: *prices* yang umum tidak pakai *the* (tapi *the price of rice* itu spesifik).

rows.en: With prices rising, people are buying less.
rows.id: Karena harga-harga terus naik, orang-orang membeli lebih sedikit.

rows.en: With the deadline approaching, the whole team worked late.
rows.id: Karena tenggat waktunya makin dekat, seluruh tim lembur.

rows.en: With the report finished, we went out for dinner.
rows.id: Karena laporannya sudah selesai, kami pergi makan malam.

rows.en: Without anyone noticing, Rina left the room.
rows.id: Tanpa ada yang menyadari, Rina keluar dari ruangan.

blocks.text: **Indonesian trap:** *dengan* can be followed by a full clause (*dengan harga yang terus naik*), so learners write *'With the prices rise'*. In English, **with** is followed by **noun + -ing** or **noun + V3**, never a full verb like *rise*, *rises* or *are rising*.

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *dengan* bisa diikuti klausa lengkap (*dengan harga yang terus naik*), jadi banyak yang menulis *'With the prices rise'*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **with** diikuti **kata benda + -ing** atau **kata benda + V3**, bukan kata kerja lengkap seperti *rise*, *rises* atau *are rising*.

blocks.prompt: With all the guests ___, the ceremony began.
blocks.explain: The guests were seated (already done): with + noun + V3 → seated. 'seat' and 'are seated' are full verbs, which can't follow with + noun.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: With all the guests ___, the ceremony began.
id.explain: Para tamu sudah duduk (sudah selesai): with + kata benda + V3 → seated. 'seat' dan 'are seated' adalah kata kerja lengkap, yang tidak bisa mengikuti with + kata benda.

id.title: with / without + kata benda + -ing atau V3

material.title: Dangling participles: who is really doing it?

blocks.text:
A participle clause has a **hidden subject**. English takes it from the main clause: the **first noun or pronoun after the comma**. If that's the wrong person or thing, the participle **dangles** (it hangs on the wrong word), and the sentence becomes funny:
- *'Arriving late, **the meeting** had already started.'* ✗ The meeting arrived late?
- *'Having been fixed by the technician, **I** could finally use my laptop.'* ✗ The technician fixed **you**?
- *'Built in 1920, **my grandfather** worked at the station.'* ✗ Your grandfather was built in 1920?
**Two ways to fix it:**
1. **Change the main subject** to the real doer: *Arriving late, **I** found that the meeting had already started.* / *Having been fixed by the technician, **my laptop** finally works again.*
2. **Use a full clause** with its own subject: ***When I arrived**, the meeting had already started.* / *My grandfather worked at the station, **which was built in 1920**.*
**C1 trap: passive main clauses.** Formal Indonesian loves *di-*: *Setelah mengecek angka-angkanya, laporan dikirim*. In English, *'Having checked the figures, **the report** was sent'* ✗ says the report checked the figures. → *Having checked the figures, **we** sent the report.* ✓

id.text:
Klausa partisip punya **subjek tersembunyi**. Bahasa Inggris mengambilnya dari klausa utama: **kata benda atau kata ganti pertama setelah koma**. Kalau itu orang atau benda yang salah, partisipnya **'menggantung'** (dangling, menempel pada kata yang salah), dan kalimatnya jadi lucu:
- *'Arriving late, **the meeting** had already started.'* ✗ Rapatnya yang datang terlambat?
- *'Having been fixed by the technician, **I** could finally use my laptop.'* ✗ Teknisi itu memperbaiki **kamu**?
- *'Built in 1920, **my grandfather** worked at the station.'* ✗ Kakekmu dibangun tahun 1920?
**Dua cara memperbaikinya:**
1. **Ganti subjek utama** dengan pelaku yang benar: *Arriving late, **I** found that the meeting had already started.* / *Having been fixed by the technician, **my laptop** finally works again.*
2. **Pakai klausa lengkap** dengan subjeknya sendiri: ***When I arrived**, the meeting had already started.* / *My grandfather worked at the station, **which was built in 1920**.*
**Jebakan C1: klausa utama pasif.** Bahasa Indonesia formal suka bentuk *di-*: *Setelah mengecek angka-angkanya, laporan dikirim*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, *'Having checked the figures, **the report** was sent'* ✗ berarti laporannya yang mengecek angka. → *Having checked the figures, **we** sent the report.* ✓

blocks.text:
**Indonesian trap:** *Setelah tiba, rapat sudah dimulai* sounds fine in Indonesian, because Indonesian lets the subject 'float'. English doesn't. Before you send a report or email, check every sentence that starts with -ing, V3 or Having: **who did it? Is that person or thing right after the comma?**
**Honest exception:** a few fixed phrases are fine even though they describe the speaker's view: *Generally speaking, …; Judging by …; Considering …* (*Judging by the queue, the new café is popular*). Remember them as phrases; they are not mistakes.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Setelah tiba, rapat sudah dimulai* terdengar wajar dalam bahasa Indonesia, karena subjeknya boleh 'mengambang'. Dalam bahasa Inggris tidak. Sebelum mengirim laporan atau email, cek setiap kalimat yang diawali -ing, V3 atau Having: **siapa yang melakukannya? Apakah orang atau benda itu ada tepat setelah koma?**
**Pengecualian yang jujur:** beberapa frasa tetap boleh dipakai walaupun menggambarkan sudut pandang pembicara: *Generally speaking, …; Judging by …; Considering …* (*Judging by the queue, the new café is popular*). Hafalkan sebagai frasa; ini bukan kesalahan.

options: Walking into the office, the smell of durian was everywhere.
Walking into the office, we noticed the smell of durian everywhere.
blocks.explain: We walked into the office, so we must come right after the comma. The first sentence says the smell of durian walked into the office.

How do I fix 'Arriving late, the meeting had already started'?

flashcards.front: Setelah diberi tahu kabar itu, dia menangis. (ringkas)
flashcards.back: Having been told the news, she started to cry.

flashcards.front: Having told vs Having been told
flashcards.back: Having told = she told someone (me-); Having been told = someone told her (di-)

flashcards.front: Karena tidak diundang, Budi tidak tahu. (not having been)
flashcards.back: Not having been invited, Budi didn't know.

flashcards.front: Didirikan tahun 2015, startup itu kini punya 200 karyawan.
flashcards.back: Founded in 2015, the startup now employs 200 people.

flashcards.front: Karena harga-harga terus naik, orang membeli lebih sedikit. (with)
flashcards.back: With prices rising, people are buying less. (not 'With the prices rise')

flashcards.front: Tanpa ada yang menyadari, Rina keluar.
flashcards.back: Without anyone noticing, Rina left the room.

flashcards.front: Arriving late, the meeting had already started. Benar?
flashcards.back: No: the meeting didn't arrive. → Arriving late, I found that… / When I arrived, …

flashcards.front: Having checked the figures, the report was sent. Benar?
flashcards.back: No: the report didn't check. → Having checked the figures, we sent the report.

id.intro: Selamat datang di C1! Di B2 kamu sudah membuka kalimat dengan -ing, V3 dan Having + V3: Walking home, I saw Rina. Having finished the report, I went home. Hari ini kita melangkah lebih jauh: Having been told the news, she… / Founded in 2015, the startup… / With prices rising, people… Kamu juga akan belajar mengenali kesalahan lucu dalam 'Arriving late, the meeting had already started'.
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya 'Having told' dan 'Having been told'?
Apakah 'Rejected twice, he…' sama dengan 'Having been rejected twice, he…'?
Kenapa 'With prices rising, people are buying less' bukan dangling participle?
Bagaimana memperbaiki 'Arriving late, the meeting had already started'?

assessment.apc-1: Tulis having atau having been di bagian kosong: ___ promoted to team leader in March, Sari now manages a team of eight.
assessment.apc-2: Lengkapi dengan having atau having been + kata kerja dalam kurung: ___ (sign) the partnership agreement, the two companies held a joint press conference in Jakarta.
assessment.apc-3: Lengkapi dengan satu kata yang dibentuk dari kata kerja dalam kurung: ___ (design) by a Dutch architect in the 1920s, the old building on our street is now a popular café.
assessment.apc-4: Lengkapi dengan satu kata yang dibentuk dari kata kerja dalam kurung: With unemployment ___ (fall) for the third year in a row, the government is under less pressure to create jobs.
assessment.apc-5:
Ada satu kata yang salah dalam kalimat ini. Tulis kata yang benar.
With interest rates go up again, many young couples are postponing their plans to buy a house.
assessment.apc-6:
Kalimat mana yang TIDAK punya dangling participle? Tulis A, B atau C.
A: Stuck in traffic for two hours, the meeting started without me.
B: Stuck in traffic for two hours, the client was told that I would be late.
C: Stuck in traffic for two hours, I missed the start of the meeting.
assessment.apc-7:
Perbaiki dangling participle ini (dalam bahasa Inggris). Pertahankan awal 'Having finished the survey,' dan jadikan the team sebagai subjek klausa utama:
Having finished the survey, the results were sent to the ministry by the team.
